note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Add a check that tells a billing specialist whether a denied claim can still be appealed. An appeal is allowed up to 120 days after the denial date, counting the denial date as day 0. After day 120 it is not allowed. Return how many days are left, or 0 when the window has closed.
facts: Made-up examples: denied on 2026-01-10, checked on 2026-03-10 gives 61 days left. Checked on 2026-05-10 (day 120) gives 0 days left but still allowed. Checked on 2026-05-11 is closed. All data is made up.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Calculate elapsed days as the number of calendar days from the denial date to the check date, with the denial date counted as day 0.
REQ-2: An appeal is allowed when elapsed days are from 0 to 120 inclusive. It is not allowed (window closed) when elapsed days exceed 120.
REQ-3: Return two outputs: an allowed/closed status, and days left. Days left equal 120 minus elapsed days when allowed, and 0 when closed. Status must be returned explicitly because 0 days left occurs both on day 120 (allowed) and after it (closed).
REQ-4: Open item, not covered by the brief: how to handle a check date earlier than the denial date. Proposed: reject as invalid input, pending requester confirmation.
AC-1: Denied 2026-01-10, checked 2026-01-10: elapsed 0, status allowed, 120 days left.
AC-2: Denied 2026-01-10, checked 2026-03-10: elapsed 59 (31 days to 2026-02-10, plus 28 days to 2026-03-10), status allowed, 61 days left.
AC-3: Denied 2026-01-10, checked 2026-05-10: elapsed 120 (59, plus 31 days to 2026-04-10, plus 30 days to 2026-05-10), status allowed, 0 days left.
AC-4: Denied 2026-01-10, checked 2026-05-11: elapsed 121, status closed, 0 days left.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: Given a denial date and a check date, tell the billing specialist whether the denied claim can still be appealed and how many days are left.
REQ-2: Count the denial date as day 0. An appeal is allowed on day 0 through day 120 inclusive and is not allowed after day 120.
REQ-3: Days left is 120 minus days elapsed since the denial date, and is 0 when the window has closed. Day 120 returns 0 days left but is still allowed.
AC-1: Denied 2026-01-10, checked 2026-03-10 is day 59, so 61 days left and the appeal is allowed.
AC-2: Denied 2026-01-10, checked 2026-05-10 is day 120, so 0 days left and the appeal is still allowed.
AC-3: Denied 2026-01-10, checked 2026-05-11 is day 121, so 0 days left and the appeal is not allowed.

reviewOfA.strengths: The draft correctly treats day 120 as still allowed with 0 days left, and its date math matches the stated examples, including 59 elapsed days and 61 days left on 2026-03-10.

reviewOfB.strengths: The acceptance criteria correctly compute 59, 120 and 121 elapsed days from 2026-01-10 (2026 is not a leap year), and they cover the inclusive day-120 boundary and the first closed day.

build.contract: checkAppealWindow(input) where input = { denialDate, checkDate } (strings, calendar dates in the form YYYY-MM-DD, such as "2026-01-10"). Returns { allowed: boolean (true when the appeal is still allowed, false when the window is closed), daysLeft: number (a whole number from 0 to 120), elapsedDays: number (a whole number of calendar days, with the denial date as day 0) }. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field, "missing field: <name>" if denialDate or checkDate is absent, and "invalid date: <name>" if either is not a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date. Pending requester confirmation of REQ-4, it also throws an Error whose message is "checkDate is before denialDate" when the check date is earlier than the denial date.

architecture.draft:
Component: one pure function, checkAppealWindow(input), with no I/O, storage or clock access. The caller always supplies checkDate, so results are repeatable.
Validation order: (1) any key other than denialDate or checkDate throws "unknown field: <name>"; (2) an absent key throws "missing field: <name>"; (3) anything that is not a real YYYY-MM-DD date throws "invalid date: <name>". Step 3 checks the shape with a regex, then confirms the date by round-tripping year, month and day, so 2026-02-30 is rejected.
Date math: convert each date to a UTC day number with Date.UTC(y, m-1, d) / 86400000, then elapsedDays = check - denial. Using UTC avoids time zone and daylight-saving off-by-one errors.
Ordering: if elapsedDays < 0, throw "checkDate is before denialDate" (REQ-4, still pending requester confirmation).
Rule: allowed = elapsedDays <= 120. daysLeft = allowed ? 120 - elapsedDays : 0. Return { allowed, daysLeft, elapsedDays }. Keep 120 as one named constant, APPEAL_WINDOW_DAYS.
Data: no persistence. Inputs are two date strings and the output is one plain object. All test data is made up.
Tests, which I checked: AC-1 gives 0 elapsed, allowed, 120 left. AC-2 gives 59 elapsed (31 + 28; 2026 is not a leap year), allowed, 61 left. AC-3 gives 120 elapsed (59 + 31 + 30), allowed, 0 left. AC-4 gives 121 elapsed, closed, 0 left. Also test each error message, plus 2026-02-29 as an invalid date.
File fence (the repo layout was not provided, so these paths are proposed): new src/appeals/checkAppealWindow.js and new tests/appeals/checkAppealWindow.test.js. No other files may change.
Out of scope: UI wiring, holidays or business-day rules, and payer-specific windows. None of these are in the brief.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Caller-supplied dates and UTC day subtraction correctly treat day 120 as allowed with 0 days left and day 121 as closed, matching all four acceptance cases.

Step 3 checks the shape with a regex, then round-trips year, month and day to reject dates such as 2026-02-30.

Rule: allowed = elapsedDays <= APPEAL_WINDOW_DAYS (120, one named constant). daysLeft = allowed ? 120 - elapsedDays : 0. Return { allowed, daysLeft, elapsedDays }.

code.summary: One pure function, checkAppealWindow({ denialDate, checkDate }). It validates in the order the architecture sets: unknown fields first, then missing fields (denialDate, then checkDate, with undefined treated as absent), then invalid dates. Date validation uses a YYYY-MM-DD regex plus a UTC round-trip, so impossible dates such as 2026-02-29 and 2026-02-30 are rejected. setUTCFullYear avoids the 0-99 year remapping that Date.UTC applies. Elapsed days are a difference of UTC day numbers, so time zones and daylight saving cannot shift the result. A check date before the denial date throws 'checkDate is before denialDate'; this is REQ-4 and still needs requester confirmation. allowed = elapsedDays <= 120 (one named constant), daysLeft = 120 - elapsedDays when allowed, else 0. I checked the acceptance criteria by hand: 2026-01-10 to 2026-01-10 = 0 elapsed, allowed, 120 left. To 2026-03-10 = 59 (21+28+10), allowed, 61 left. To 2026-05-10 = 120 (21+28+31+30+10), allowed, 0 left. To 2026-05-11 = 121, closed, 0 left. One assumption: a non-object input is treated as empty and throws 'missing field: denialDate'. All data is made up.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: UTC calendar-day subtraction keeps the denial date as day 0 and treats day 120 as allowed with 0 days left, matching the acceptance cases.

diagram.summary: A billing specialist enters a claim's denial date and check date into existing calling code, which passes them to a new pure function; the function validates the dates, counts elapsed UTC days against the 120-day window, and returns whether an appeal is allowed and how many days remain.
